absent: Complete layouts, widths and alignment of scheduler structures beyond members observed in these fragments.
Lock ordering, nesting and interrupt context rules across runqueues, domains and bandwidth objects beyond the single critical sections shown.
Full lifecycle and concurrency semantics of replenish and inactive timers including expiry paths not routed here.
Clearing paths for overload indicators and migration pull logic that consumes the published masks and counts.
Configuration conditions selecting among alternate empty versus active helper variants.
Numeric values, units and bounds for priorities, bandwidth, slices, epochs and tolerance parameters.

findings.text: A globally reachable updater changes the priority associated with a given CPU, publishing the new per-priority membership before withdrawing the old one, and leaving state untouched when the converted value equals the current one.
A globally reachable remover withdraws a CPU from the deadline-ordered heap when present, compacts occupancy, restores ordering, and reflects online status in the free set.
Small cross-file helpers adjust deadline bandwidth reservations, maintain the per-runqueue deadline count, and cancel the replenishment timer for an entity.

Runqueue occupancy helpers raise or lower the runnable count with tracing and tick-dependency refresh, alongside accessors that read or conditionally update the root-domain overload flag and a thin trace forwarder.

Published helpers expose the averaged virtual-time value, shift the virtual-time origin, perform cache-aware execution accounting, record wait-start statistics, and report whether real-time bandwidth remains available.
Descendant positions in the binary heap follow a fixed doubling scheme where each side uses its own offset, giving a deterministic layout for sift operations.

The deadline heap keeps the earliest deadline near the top with a per-CPU back index that stays coherent with slot occupancy, tolerating attempts to sift a leaf or withdraw an absent CPU without disturbance.

Priority reassignment makes the new membership visible before dropping the old one, with store ordering between mask and counter updates so concurrent scanners observe at least one association during raises.

Incoming scheduler priorities map into a compact priority space where a distinguished invalid code is preserved, a contiguous low range is mirrored inversely, and boundary values collapse to dedicated normal and higher codes.

The fragments show the root-domain flag being raised when occupancy grows beyond a single runnable with no lowering in the same helpers, while deadline overload membership is installed only on first pushable arrival.

Tick-dependency maintenance exists in build-dependent forms, one that conditions the scheduler dependency bit on full-tickless state and stoppability and one that does nothing, invoked after occupancy changes.

Deadline dequeue always detaches the entity from its ordered tree when linked, and additionally releases bandwidth reservations or triggers the non-contending transition only when the corresponding dequeue reasons are present.
After removal the cached earliest deadline reflects the leftmost remaining entity, or is cleared together with the global deadline and priority trackers when no deadline entity remains.

A blocking or terminating deadline entity either reclaims active utilization immediately when its lag horizon has passed or a reclaim is already pending, or is marked non-contending with a timed reclaim armed; entities without runtime or with special status are left alone.
Pushable deadline tasks live in a deadline-ordered tree with a cached successor deadline, and the first insertion arms runqueue overload; offline runqueues never publish overload.

Enqueueing a deadline task reconciles boost and throttle conditions, refreshes wait statistics, propagates migrating state, and admits only suitable non-current throttle-free migratable tasks to the pushable set, with de-boosted non-deadline tasks taking an early path that clears throttle.

Scheduling statistics and their requirement checks compile to either active accounting with dependency warnings or inert no-ops, with wait-start recording keyed off the runqueue clock and prior values.

Fair time scaling leaves baseline-weighted deltas unchanged and otherwise applies weight-proportional adjustment through either a cached-inverse fixed-point form or a direct ratio form, with lazy initialization handling empty and saturating weights.

Virtual-time ordering uses signed differences with support for ordered relational forms and a build-time failure for others, underpinning slice protection and deadline renewal that extends the deadline by a weight-adjusted slice and refreshes the average.

The averaged virtual time blends queued weight and the current entity when present, corrects for sign when forming the delta, and advances the origin while re-basing the weighted sum so future keys stay relative.

Execution accounting measures elapsed task-clock time since the last stamp, attributes it to the running task under proxy execution or to the entity otherwise, and refreshes maxima and group plus memory plus cgroup observers.

Cache-aware accounting runs only for fair non-kernel threads with an assigned group and per-CPU state, accumulating runtime under epoch protection, invalidating stale preferred placement, and comparing scaled last-level capacity against footprint with a tolerance-driven bypass.
Real-time admission reports availability when the period timer is active or consumed time remains below the group runtime, resolved through the entity group bandwidth.
Blocked status is negative unless proxy execution is enabled, in which case it mirrors whether the task has a blocking dependency.

The deadline CPU heap comprises a sized slot array holding per-slot CPU identity and deadline, a reverse index from CPU to slot with a distinguished absent marker, occupancy size, exclusion state, and a free-CPU set.
The priority tracker comprises a per-CPU current-value array plus a per-priority vector array where each vector pairs a CPU membership set with a live occupancy counter.

Deadline runqueue state pairs an ordered tree and runnable count with cached current and successor deadlines and a pushable tree plus overload flag, while each entity carries tree linkage, deadline and timing parameters, bandwidth share, throttle and contention flags, and inactive and replenish timers.

Fair runqueue state aggregates the current entity, total and weighted virtual-time sums, origin and shift, while each entity carries virtual time, protection point, deadline, slice and custom-slice marker, hierarchical load, execution stamps and totals, and queue membership.

Cache grouping state links a task to a group with per-CPU timing storage, epoch and preferred CPU and footprint, while runqueue state carries epoch, accumulated runtime and exclusion, and tasks carry a preferred last-level location.
Deadline heap mutation and free-set updates occur under a single irq-saving exclusion held across index lookup, compaction, reordering and mask change.
Global deadline bandwidth adjustment is serialized by the bandwidth exclusion, and cache runtime accumulation with epoch sampling is serialized by the runqueue epoch exclusion with scoped release.
Priority and overload publication rely on ordered writes between membership and counter with pairing barriers rather than a common lock, requiring add-before-remove and mask-before-count discipline.

A deadline entity moves among queued, throttled, boosted, non-contending with armed timer, and inactive or parameter-cleared outcomes, with server entities following a reduced reclaim path and timers mediating delayed transitions.

Overload and tick dependencies evolve monotonically in these fragments: root overload is raised on growth, deadline overload is set on first pushable arrival, and the scheduler tick dependency is set or cleared according to stoppability, with clearing of overloads defined elsewhere.

Queue and dequeue handlers for deadline tasks serve as scheduling-class entry points that validate boost state, maintain statistics and bandwidth, update global trackers, and manage pushable membership.

Reversing publication order or omitting pairing barriers risks a CPU being missed during priority scans, while concurrent replenish expiry, inactive-timer activity, and offline transitions require tolerance for already-absent or already-armed states.

Edge inputs include empty trees needing recomputation guards, zero or saturating weights needing dedicated inverse handling, unknown comparison operators failing at build time, and wrap-sensitive signed virtual-time differences.
The priority translation exposes distinct codes for invalid, normal and higher levels with an inverse mapping over the low real-time range and a bound on the number of priority vectors.
Named reason flags distinguish save, migrating and sleep removals from replenish and migrating insertions, and a dedicated scheduler bit names the tick dependency.
